thread:
sam_cs: :rotating_light: Heads-up — Banyan onboarding tests generated an unexpected dedicated GPU queue spike overnight. We're seeing sustained queue depth and latency regressions. Can infra/sre triage?

capacity-bot: Auto-report: pool=banyan-reserved-1, window=01:00-04:00 UTC, avg_gpu_hours=18.2 (baseline 7.8), peak_queue_depth=42, 95p_latency_tokens=320ms -> 980ms, error_rate(5m)=3.4% (mainly 429/503). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/banyan/pool-health

mika_infra: on it — pulling logs now. initial look: many short-lived burst sessions from onboarding script, no single job hogging gpus. probs batching pattern.

harpreet_sre: saw fallback to smaller model for some requests -> increased RT for clients. 429s are coming from our request-queue throttling layer, not the tenant. Also noticed KV-cache miss rate spiked after test resets.

jess_am: flagged on my side — Banyan has a 3pm enablement call today; they might notice. if this impacts their SLA we should offer a brief remediation update. Renewal risk: low->medium for this week unless we contain spend.

sam_cs: proposed immediate actions: 1) temporary throttle onboarding script by setting per-tenant concurrency cap, 2) enable prefix/KV warm for their demo model, 3) open prioritization ticket for dedicated slot during next tests, 4) notify Finance to watch burst charges. Agree? :+1:

mika_infra: agree. I can apply a soft cap now: run `redwoodctl capacity update --tenant banyan --concurrency 8 --window 2h` to limit burst. applying in 2 mins.

```
# quick command we will run
redwoodctl capacity update --tenant banyan --concurrency 8 --window 2h --reason "onboarding spike mitigation"
```

harpreet_sre: also toggling conservative autoscale rules for that pool so we avoid aggressive spinups that we can't refill: `scale.policy=banyan-onboard-conservative` — will monitor error rate and latency for 15m after change.

ops-bot: Action: capacity cap applied by mika_infra at 1719992350. Autoscale policy set to banyan-onboard-conservative by harpreet_sre at 1719992405.

jess_am: I'm going to tell the customer we've applied a temporary cap and that we'll walk them through batching/kv-warm best practices on the call. Can someone prep a 5-min deck / bullet list?

sam_cs: I'll draft bullets. Key notes: reduce per-request parallelism during demos, pre-warm KV with `prefill_cache=true`, recommend `max_tokens` tuning.

mika_infra: initial metric deltas after cap (5m): peak_queue_depth down -> 18, 95p_latency_tokens -> 420ms, error_rate -> 0.9%. Looks promising but we need 30-60m stability.

harpreet_sre: opening internal ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/CS-8721 "Banyan onboarding queue & mitigation" — assigned to mika_infra, target P1 triage for next 24h.

ops-bot: Billing alert sent to finance-team@redwood for potential burst spend anomaly (tenant: banyan, est_overage=$1.2k).

jess_am: noted. I'll loop in CSM renewal lead to monitor.

sam_cs: Summary / next steps: - temporary concurrency cap applied (mika) - autoscale conservative policy applied (harpreet) - ticket CS-8721 opened, owner=mika - enablement call 15:00 UTC: prep by sam/jess (5-min best-practices) - finance alerted about possible overage. Check back in 60m for stability update. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

mika_infra: 60m update -> stability holding, queue depth 10-15, latency steady ~400ms, errors ~0.5%. I'll keep the cap for 2h then re-evaluate with SRE/CS.

harpreet_sre: keeping monitor on. If KV-miss remains high we'll recommend small TTL change for their prefill routine.

sam_cs: thanks team. I'll give Banyan a short status note now and go into the call prepared.

jess_am: thanks all :clap: follow-ups in CS-8721.
